blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). The r418-r421 shutdown hang is FIXED and LIVE-VERIFIED (r422), with automated regression coverage added (r424). r423 was a traceability correction on r422's commit scope (no technical change). Separate, not-yet-fixed discovery from r424: HEAD has never been buildable from a byte-for-byte fresh clone (native_vulkan_backend.cpp has never had Vulkan linkage in any committed CMakeLists.txt) -- named for a dedicated future cycle, not a blocker for anything in this chain since the working tree already has the missing pieces on disk. r425 made real progress on the next open PRODUCT question (presented_frames=0/present=0, r418): confirmed for the first time that VdSwap -- the real Xbox 360 kernel present call -- IS called by the guest (5x/25s, via the same sustained per-frame-loop chain r417 already characterized), and that its validation path (native_guest_vd.cpp's publish_write_address, already instrumented by earlier pre-r399 cycles r295/r296) does sometimes find and drain genuinely new ring content (1 of 5 calls this cycle: 'vd swap commit' fired, drained 12 dwords of real content -- 4 draws, 13 waits, 4 event writes, 6 immediate shaders). Even then, present=0 in that batch -- and a separate, later background-poller-drained batch reached 50 real draws with still zero Present packets. This closes the r292-r296 'ring discovery might be buggy' hypothesis: discovery and draining both work correctly when there is new content: the guest genuinely never writes a PM4 XE_SWAP opcode (native_xenos.cpp:401, kOpcodeXeSwap/kSwapSignature) into its own command stream in the observed window, despite calling VdSwap and despite rendering real geometry. Named for r426: read sub_821F03B0 (VdSwap's direct caller, never read) to find where/whether the guest builds an XE_SWAP packet before calling VdSwap, and whether its structure matches what the PM4 decoder expects. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond what r422 already swept in -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r425 were committed individually.
